posts.text: 🌲 - 🇱🇧 🇱🇧 A senior Lebanese judicial source said that the five suspected Hezbollah operatives arrested in the Batroun–Bsharri highlands gave contradictory explanations during interrogation, initially claiming they were buying a car, then organizing food assistance, and later preparing for possible wartime displacement. Investigators recovered documents listing Kalashnikov rifles, RPG-7 rocket launchers, snipers, ambushes, and mines across northern Lebanon. The detainees' families told investigators that members of Hezbollah's security committee collected their mobile phones shortly after the arrests became public, preventing authorities from examining the devices. The five defendants are expected to appear before Military Investigating Judge Ghada Abou Alwan on November 19.

Open Source Intel Poland's constitutional crisis has escalated. At the heart of it is a battle for control of the Constitutional Tribunal. On one side is the pro-European government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk. On the other are the nationalist opposition and President Karol Nawrocki. The tribunal's judges voted to remove the immunity of Bogdan Święczkowski, the court's ousted president. He can now be prosecuted on suspicion of exceeding his authority and unauthorized use of classified information. Święczkowski was appointed by the previous right-wing conservative government. He was suspended in October. He calls his removal illegal and accuses Tusk of an attempted coup. Polish PM Donald Tusk: Together with the parliamentary majority, I made attempts to repair the Tribunal. No one had any doubt that the Tribunal in the form imposed by PiS was not a real court. That was the assessment of international institutions, Polish legal authorities and public opinion. - Open Source Intel tweet

Salah a-Din road, Gaza's main north-south highway, will be closed in the area during the raid.
